aspects.says: A generated accessor whose name and type match an interface method implements it, with no body needed.
basis: section:A Record's Body Adds Methods, Static Members and Interfaces, but No Instance Field

aspects.says: An array component is mutable, so a record that must not change copies it on the way in and on the way out.
basis: section:A Record's equals Compares Each Component with Its Own equals, So an Array Compares by Identity

aspects.says: Every other constructor must start with this(...), so every way of making a record ends in the canonical constructor, and a check placed anywhere else guards only one path.
basis: section:A Custom Constructor Must Call the Canonical One First, So Checks Belong in the Canonical One

aspects.says: A value assigned to a parameter in the compact constructor is the value stored, so equals, hashCode and the accessor all see it.
basis: section:The Compact Constructor Runs Before the Fields Are Assigned, So It Checks the Parameters

aspects.says: A compact constructor's body runs before the fields are assigned, so accessors and other instance methods called there see default values; checks read the parameters.
basis: section:The Compact Constructor Runs Before the Fields Are Assigned, So It Checks the Parameters
section:Spot the Problem: a Check That Never Fires

aspects.says: Deserializing a record calls its canonical constructor and no other, so a check in another constructor doesn't run.
basis: section:A Custom Constructor Must Call the Canonical One First, So Checks Belong in the Canonical One

aspects.says: A record's generated equals and hashCode use each component's own equals and hashCode, so an array component compares by identity and two records holding equal arrays are not equal.
basis: section:A Record's equals Compares Each Component with Its Own equals, So an Array Compares by Identity

aspects.says: Nested and local records are implicitly static, so they can't read an enclosing instance's fields or a method's local variables; such values become components.
basis: section:Nested and Local Records Are Static, So They Can't Reach an Outer Instance or a Local Variable

aspects.says: A record's body may declare static fields, static and instance methods and nested types, but no instance field.
basis: section:A Record's Body Adds Methods, Static Members and Interfaces, but No Instance Field
